-71.10670,42.33620.name: Brigham and Women's Hospital Center for Assisted Reproductive Technology
-71.10670,42.33620.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. Medical director: Serene S. Srouji, MD. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

-1.62055,54.96766.name: Newcastle Fertility Centre at Life
-1.62055,54.96766.state: International Centre for Life, Bioscience Centre, Times Square, Newcastle upon Tyne, NE1 4EP, United Kingdom
-1.62055,54.96766.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-113.52449,53.52682.name: University of Alberta
-113.52449,53.52682.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, March 2024
-113.52449,53.52682.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. Certificate of GAP Last visit: regular, March 2024. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-89.19116,13.69763.name: Latid Fertility Center
-89.19116,13.69763.desc: A centre accredited by REDLARA, the Latin American Network of Assisted Reproduction. Website: https://www.latidfertilitycenter.com/. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. REDLARA accreditation is voluntary and its members report to a shared registry, which is why Latin America can be read at all — most countries in the region have no national register of clinics. What it is not is a complete list: a clinic outside REDLARA appears nowhere. No street address resolved, so this point is the city or the country rather than the centre.

-75.49000,40.61200.name: Ace Animals / laboratory dog and cat supply
-75.49000,40.61200.state: Boyertown, Pennsylvania — Ace Animals, 2 Rittenhouse Rd
-75.49000,40.61200.desc: A Class A dealer breeding dogs and cats for research, licensed and inspected by USDA APHIS. Purpose-bred beagles are the standard dog in toxicology because regulators require a non-rodent species for most safety studies, so the requirement itself creates the market. Class B dealers, who bought animals from random sources including pounds, were phased out of live-animal supply after sustained investigation; Class A breeding replaced them, which resolved the provenance question and not the underlying one.

6.42700,51.19000.name: Qiagen
6.42700,51.19000.desc: Sample preparation and nucleic acid extraction kits, used before nearly every sequencing run, plus a forensic genomics line. Extraction is the invisible step on which every result downstream depends, and two or three companies supply almost all of it.

174.77000,-36.85000.name: AsureQuality
174.77000,-36.85000.desc: A New Zealand government-owned company selling food assurance commercially: laboratories, auditing, organic certification, and the country's recognised meat inspection agency. It is a recognised agency for the Ministry for Primary Industries to provide third-party assurance where government-to-government official assurance is required — so a state function is discharged by a company the state owns and which competes for the same work commercially. It markets its government ownership as a selling point for its organic mark. In the same domestic market BioGro certifies for export and domestic sale, and OrganicFarmNZ offers lower-cost certification for smaller producers selling only domestically: three tiers, one of them owned by the regulator's own shareholder.
